facts.fact: The EastAfrican, on the IIAG 2026, says Uganda's Computer Misuse Act (2011, amended 2022) is in operation, and that in March 2026 the Constitutional Court struck down several provisions of the 2022 amendments on procedural and free-expression grounds.

facts.fact: The EastAfrican says Tanzania's internet and communication slowdowns around major political and judicial events, such as the 6 November 2026 sentencing of Chadema leader Tundu Lissu, are part of a recurring pattern of state-managed bandwidth throttling.
The EastAfrican lists Uganda among countries where governments used internet shutdowns, social media throttling and platform blockades around the 2026 general elections.

The EastAfrican says that in March 2026 Uganda's Constitutional Court struck down several provisions of the 2022 Computer Misuse Act amendments, including those on hate speech and social media misuse, for violating free expression.
